# Determinant characters for split products of Frobenius-truncated algebras

This note answers the split-product part of the open question in
[Ali Romman's PR5637](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5637).
The local factor models and a decomposition certificate are supplied. We
derive their product's automorphism determinant image, full covariant tensor
stabilizer image, special-linear orbit label and constructive transporters.
We do not recognize an arbitrary tensor or recover a decomposition from it.
The result is an algebraic interface statement and does not improve kappa.

## 1. Models and the main formula

Fix one explicit finite field K = F_q of characteristic p. All algebra
automorphisms and tensor factor maps below are K-linear; coefficient-field
automorphisms are not allowed. Let s >= 1
and define

    B_j = K[x_(j,1),...,x_(j,r_j)] / (x_(j,i)^(p^h_(j,i))),
    A = product_(j=1)^s B_j,
    N_j = dim_K B_j = p^(sum_i h_(j,i)),
    n = dim_K A = sum_j N_j.

Each height is a positive integer. An empty height list means B_j = K
and N_j = 1. A factor's **type** is its sorted height list. Within a factor,
use the monomial basis with lexicographically ordered exponent tuples. The
canonical product model orders factor types lexicographically; equal types
are consecutive copies of the same model.

Set L = q-1, and for every variable define the integer

    E_(j,i) = N_j * (p^h_(j,i) - 1) / 2.

It is integral: for odd p the second factor is even; for p = 2 every factor
containing a variable has even dimension. Include a swap generator precisely
when q is odd and some type occurs at least twice with odd component
dimension. Its exponent is T = L/2. Set

    g = gcd(L, all E_(j,i), T if that swap generator exists),
    H_g = {c^g : c in K*}.

The gcd of the singleton list (L) is L. This includes field factors with
empty height lists and q = 2, where L = g = 1. Every N_j in this family is
odd when q is odd; the dimension condition identifies the sign's source.

**Theorem.** The image of Aut_K(A) under determinant is exactly H_g. For
multiplication mu_A and the covariant action on A* tensor A* tensor A, the
full stabilizer determinant image is

    Delta(mu_A) = {(u,v,w) in (K*)^3 : uvw in H_g}
                = {(u,v,w) : (uvw)^(L/g) = 1}.

It has L^3/g elements. The general-linear orbit of mu_A contains exactly g
orbits under SL_n(K)^3. Every allowed determinant triple is attained by an
explicit autotopism. For tensors supplied with verified factor maps, the
canonical type multiset and Section 6's label completely decide
special-linear equivalence.

## 2. Local type and local determinant character

We restate the local argument of PR5459 to identify the input to the product
calculation. In B = K[x_1,...,x_r]/(x_i^(p^h_i)), let J = (x_1,...,x_r).
An element with nonzero constant term is a unit by a finite geometric
series; all elements of J are nilpotent. Thus B is local with residue field
K. Its only idempotents are zero and one: one of e and 1-e is a unit, and
e(1-e) = 0 determines an idempotent e.

The tangent quotient J/J^2 has the variables as a basis. Its intrinsic
height flag is

    V_e = (ker(a -> a^(p^e)) + J^2)/J^2.

These kernels are K-subspaces even though the power map is semilinear over
an extension field. Frobenius removes mixed terms. A nonzero linear term
in x_i survives the p^e power exactly when h_i > e, and no term of degree
at least two can cancel its degree-p^e monomial. Therefore V_e is exactly
the span of variables of height at most e. Its dimension increments recover
the height multiset. Two displayed local factors are isomorphic if and only
if their types agree; equal dimension alone is insufficient.

An automorphism's tangent map preserves this flag. Conversely, an invertible
flag-preserving linear substitution respects the defining power relations:
a variable of height h is sent only to variables whose heights are at most
h. Its inverse preserves the same flag, so this substitution is an
automorphism. A general automorphism and its linear substitution induce the
same map on the associated graded algebra for powers of J. A monomial basis
ordered by total degree shows that they have equal determinants.

The flag-preserving group is generated by allowed elementary substitutions
and diagonal scalings. For an allowed substitution x_i -> x_i + c*x_k,
the monomial expansion is triangular when ordered by x_i exponent, with
diagonal one. Its determinant is one. Scaling x_i -> c*x_i has determinant
c^E_i: the sum of the x_i exponents over the N monomials is

    E_i = N * (p^h_i - 1) / 2.

Elementary and diagonal matrices generate the full general-linear group
within each equal-height block, while the other allowed elementary matrices
generate the off-diagonal flag-preserving part. Thus the local determinant
image is generated exactly by the subgroups {c^E_i : c in K*}. With an empty
height list, the K-algebra K has only the identity automorphism.

## 3. Primitive idempotents and the permutation contribution

An idempotent of A has each coordinate zero or one. The nonzero primitive
idempotents are precisely the e_j supported on a single factor: any
idempotent supported on more than one factor splits into nonzero orthogonal
idempotents. Algebra automorphisms preserve this intrinsic property.

An automorphism sending e_j to e_k restricts to an isomorphism e_j A -> e_k A,
so those factors have the same type. Conversely, any permutation among
copies of one type, together with an independent automorphism on each factor,
defines an automorphism of A. These are all the possibilities; there are
no additional maps mixing primitive factors.

Factorwise automorphisms contribute the product of their local determinants.
Swapping two identical factors of dimension N swaps N pairs of matching
basis vectors, so its determinant is (-1)^N. This remains true for blocks
separated by other blocks: those same N basis-vector transpositions describe
the operation. Equivalently, conjugate by a fixed reordering that places the
copies together. For any allowed permutation the sign contribution is

    product_over_types type_permutation_sign^(dimension_of_that_type).

Hence signs contribute only for repeated isomorphic odd-dimensional factors
in odd characteristic. In characteristic two every sign is one. Unequal
types cannot be swapped, even when they have the same dimension.

The finite group K* is cyclic of order L. Relative to a generator zeta, the
determinant generators have exponents E_(j,i) and, when present, T = L/2.
They generate precisely <zeta^g> = H_g. Each generator is attained by a
literal variable scaling or permitted block transposition. This proves
the automorphism image and its attainment.

## 4. Unit determinants and the full tensor stabilizer

For a unit a = (a_j), multiplication by a_j is triangular on its monomials
ordered by total degree. Its constant term c_j is on every diagonal entry.
Consequently

    det(L_a) = product_j c_j^N_j.

This map is onto K*: choose one component and let all other components
equal one. The chosen N_j is a power of p and is coprime to L, so its scalar
constant can attain any desired determinant. For q = 2 the unit one suffices.
This uses one component dimension N_j, not the total dimension n, which
need not be coprime to L.

We use the classical unital commutative autotopism normalization retained in
PR5252 and PR5459. Suppose invertible F,G,H satisfy

    F(x) * G(y) = H(x*y).

Put a = F(1), b = G(1). Evaluation at one gives H(x) = F(x)*b = a*G(x).
Invertibility of F,G,H implies that multiplication by a and b is invertible,
so a and b are units. Then sigma = L_(ab)^(-1) H is a unital algebra
automorphism and

    F = L_a sigma,   G = L_b sigma,   H = L_(ab) sigma.

Conversely these maps always form an autotopism. Write x = det L_a,
y = det L_b, z = det sigma. The corresponding covariant stabilizer element
is (F^(-T),G^(-T),H), with determinant triple

    (u,v,w) = (x^(-1) z^(-1), y^(-1) z^(-1), x*y*z).

Its product is z^(-1), in H_g. Conversely, for a requested triple with
uvw in H_g, set

    z = (u*v*w)^(-1),   x = v*w,   y = u*w.

The automorphism and unit determinant constructions attain these three
values and hence the requested triple. This proves the full image formula.
There are L^2 choices for the first two entries and L/g possible products,
so its cardinality is L^3/g.

## 5. Constructive determinant witnesses

Fix a generator zeta of K*. For a desired z in H_g, write z = zeta^k
with 0 <= k < L; membership is equivalent to g dividing k. Bezout
coefficients give

    g = b_0 L + sum_(j,i) b_(j,i) E_(j,i) + b_T T,

omitting the final term when no swap generator exists. Scale variable (j,i)
by zeta^(b_(j,i)*k/g), and compose one fixed permitted transposition to
power b_T*k/g if needed. The resulting determinant is z. Negative
coefficients are allowed because the maps are invertible. If all character
generators are trivial, only z = 1 is requested and the identity suffices.

For desired unit determinant x, choose a component j and an inverse r of
N_j modulo L. The unit with scalar x^r in that component and one elsewhere
has determinant x. In the trivial multiplicative group use the identity.
Together with Section 4 this constructs every allowed determinant triple.

Primitive-element and discrete-log enumeration in an explicit finite field
suffice for a fixed q. This is not a polynomial bit-complexity claim in log q.
A different exact subgroup witness search can be used, provided it verifies
the same determinants and transported basis products.

## 6. Supplied certificates and special-linear labels

A tensor t: K^n x K^n -> K^n is supplied with model factor types and three
invertible matrices U,V,W, in the convention

    t(U*a,V*b) = W*mu_A(a,b).

Columns are basis images from the declared model to the tensor. Check the
dimensions, invertibility and all n^2 model basis products. By bilinearity
these finite identities verify the supplied decomposition for all inputs.
They do not provide a procedure for discovering the certificate.

The reference model must be fixed before comparing labels. Heights inside
each factor are sorted, and factor types are sorted lexicographically.
For another supplied component order, construct the monomial permutation
R from the canonical model to the supplied model, matching full types and
monomial coordinates. Normalize the factor maps to

    U_c = U*R,   V_c = V*R,   W_c = W*R.

Thus, with d_raw = det(W)/(det(U)*det(V)),

    d = det(W_c)/(det(U_c)*det(V_c)) = d_raw/det(R),
    label(t) = d^(L/g).

Sorting type metadata alone can lose this permutation sign. If variable
order is also changed inside a supplied factor, its monomial permutation
must also be included, or the interface must require sorted heights from
the start. R changes the reference model coordinates, not the ambient
coordinates of t.

Two choices of matching among identical factors differ by a model
automorphism, whose determinant lies in H_g, so the label is unchanged.
More generally, two valid certificates from the same canonical model differ
by a tensor stabilizer. Their determinant products differ by an element of
H_g. The label is therefore independent of the certificate.

For completeness, let G = GL_n(K)^3 and S = SL_n(K)^3. The determinant map
G -> (K*)^3 has kernel S. Since S is normal, its orbits within a fixed
G-orbit correspond to cosets of the stabilizer determinant image. The product
map identifies these cosets with K*/H_g. The map d -> d^(L/g) has kernel
H_g, so its value is a complete label, with exactly g possible values.

Different type multisets cannot be general-linearly equivalent. An isotopy
between multiplication in two unital commutative algebras normalizes exactly
as in Section 4, using units in the target algebra, to an algebra isomorphism.
It must match primitive idempotents and then local types. Conversely a type
matching gives a literal product algebra isomorphism. For verified
certificates over the same explicit field, therefore,

    SL-equivalent iff canonical type multisets agree and labels agree.

Different presentations of the finite field need an explicit, checked field
isomorphism before their element-valued labels can be compared.

## 7. Determinant-one transporters

Let two normalized certificates (U_1,V_1,W_1) and (U_2,V_2,W_2) have the
same canonical model and label. Put

    a = det(U_1)/det(U_2),
    b = det(V_1)/det(V_2),
    c = det(W_1)/det(W_2).

We need a model autotopism (P,Q,R_0) with determinants (a,b,c). In
Section 4's notation choose

    z = a*b/c,   x = a/z,   y = b/z.

Equal labels imply (c/(a*b))^(L/g) = 1, hence z belongs to H_g.
Section 5 constructs the required automorphism and units. Then

    F = U_2 * P   * U_1^(-1),
    G = V_2 * Q   * V_1^(-1),
    H = W_2 * R_0 * W_1^(-1)

all have determinant one and satisfy

    t_2(F*x,G*y) = H*t_1(x,y).

Substitution in the certificate identities proves this. An executable can
also verify the three determinants and every transported basis product.
Unequal labels preclude such maps.

## 8. Discriminating examples and boundary cases

Over F_3, let B = F_3[x]/(x^9). Its height list is (2), dimension nine,
and local exponent 9*(9-1)/2 = 36. Since L = 2, the local automorphism
determinant image is {1}; its multiplication orbit splits into two
special-linear orbits. For B x B, a block transposition has determinant
(-1)^9 = -1. The product gcd is gcd(2,36,36,1) = 1, giving only one
special-linear orbit. A product rule using only local characters misses
this change.

The factors F_3[x]/(x^9) and F_3[y,z]/(y^3,z^3) both have dimension nine,
but their height lists (2) and (1,1) have different tangent dimensions.
A proposed swap is not an algebra automorphism. Equal component size
does not authorize a permutation generator or component match.

If all heights are empty, A = K^s. For s = 1 the automorphism image is
trivial and g = L. For s >= 2 and odd q, permutations add -1 and g = L/2;
in characteristic two they add nothing and g = L. This agrees with the
split finite-etale case of PR5252. For q = 2 every nonzero determinant and
label is one, and g = 1 for every model.

Unequal component dimensions add no automorphism generators, but their block
ordering still affects normalization of a supplied certificate. The empty
product and zero-dimensional zero algebra are excluded. An empty height
list inside a nonempty product is a valid field factor.

## 9. Cost, credit and remaining obligations

The gcd formula only needs exponents modulo L. Compute
p^(sum_i h_(j,i)) * (p^h_(j,i)-1) modulo 2L and halve its even residue
to obtain E_(j,i) modulo L without materializing a large component dimension.
Modular powers, type comparison and gcd are polynomial in the parameter bit
lengths, given p,q and the finite-field contract. Building and checking
explicit matrices is instead polynomial in the explicit algebra dimension
at fixed q. These are different size statements: a short symbolic height
list can specify an algebra too large to materialize. The executable builds
literal model dimensions and local exponents; the modular method just
described is an arithmetic consequence of the formula, not an implemented
compressed-model runtime guarantee.

Ali Romman's [PR5459 at bef3575ddb19c44434a7e2460a353eac7c4d9387](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bef3575ddb19c44434a7e2460a353eac7c4d9387/research/frobenius-tensor-characters/README.md)
supplies the local height flag and determinant character; those local
results are predecessor work. His
[PR5637 at 86389e525d3efafe236e929f6ae401c68be1d115](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/86389e525d3efafe236e929f6ae401c68be1d115/research/extension-field-tensor-recognition/README.md)
supplies extension-field recognition, local special-linear labels and the
explicit product handoff. [apoursh's PR5502](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5502)
supplies the prime-field table height criterion.
[Nick Petalas's PR5252](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5252)
supplies finite-etale tensor determinants and the normalization lineage.
David Ganz and the retained atlas framework retain their credit. Primitive
idempotents, cyclic subgroup arithmetic and unital isotopy normalization are
classical; no general literature-priority claim is made.

Open next questions are recovery of this decomposition from an arbitrary
tensor and local factors with residue fields larger than the base. The
latter requires coefficient-field identifications, norms and additional
automorphisms; it does not follow by dropping the residue-field hypothesis.
Neither task is supplied here. Physical coefficient preparation, native
implementation, precision, movement, restoration, supplier admission and
a new multiplication exponent remain outside this result.

The written theorem covers general finite fields. Executable coverage is
limited to the field contract and domains stated in the package's README;
finite checks are corroboration, not a proof-kernel verification.
